title: Marimo RCE Flaw Lets Hackers Steal AWS Credentials and Pivot to Bastion Host in 8 Seconds
content_md: A threat actor exploited a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in marimo to harvest AWS credentials, retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager, and authenticate to a bastion host in eight seconds. Tracked as CVE-2026-39987, the vulnerability affects marimo versions through 0.20.4. The flaw stems from missing authentication on /terminal/ws , exposing an interactive PTY shell to remote clients able to connect. Marimo version 0.23.0 fixes the issue by adding the missing authentication validation. Sysdig observed the operator use the access to run an end-to-end cloud pivot chain during a nine-hour intrusion. Marimo RCE Flaw The attacker opened a WebSocket session, recovered AWS credentials from the compromised notebook environment and its Redis-backed application data , called Secrets Manager, wrote a private key to /tmp/bastion_key , and used it to access an internet-facing bastion. At 18:57:22 UTC, a WebSocket session began. Four seconds later, the attacker recovered an AWS key from the application’s stored credentials. At 18:57:30, SSH authentication to the bastion was recorded. The compressed sequence shows how quickly a prepared toolkit can turn notebook compromise into deeper cloud access. Unlike previously tracked operators exploiting the same bug, this actor appeared to rely on hand-built automation rather than LLM-generated tooling. Over several hours, they dropped base64-encoded Python scripts into /tmp/ and iteratively refined boto3 and SSH routine
